title: Maximal convergence speed of decentralized control
journal: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
summary_en: Simonovits derives the maximal speed at which a decentralised control mechanism — where local managers update their decisions based only on partial signals — can converge to the system's steady state. The paper extends the linear control-theory toolkit to decentralised settings and provides upper bounds on convergence speed as a function of the network of information links between managers. The results clarify when decentralisation imposes a real efficiency cost relative to the central planner's benchmark.
data_used: Theoretical model — no dataset. Linear-system analysis of decentralised adjustment dynamics.
policy_relevance: Continued mathematical-econ heritage of the Hungarian School. Less directly relevant to today's policy debates, but underpins later applied work by Simonovits and coauthors on Hungarian pension-system dynamics and adjustment lags. Useful background for understanding the analytic style behind KRTK pension modelling.
